_doc: THE PRESERVATION CORPUS -- the data half of the document-level invariant
edit through a production path and both active ports assert the same six
document-level invariants over the canonical test JSON before and after.
WHY THIS FILE IS AN OBJECT AND NOT A BARE ARRAY. Until 2026-07-28 it was a
top-level list, and emptying it to `[]` turned ALL FOUR of its gates green:
the two ports' gates are `for` loops over the array with no floor, and
scripts/check_corpus_manifest.py never fired because the DIRECTORY was
still non-empty. Deleting the file or the directory was caught; emptying
it was not. `min_vectors` closes that: it is a fact the corpus states
ABOUT ITSELF, so the floor lives in one place instead of as a magic number
in four, and lowering it is a visible edit to this header rather than an
invisible deletion of data. Every one of the four gates reads it and
refuses a corpus that carries fewer vectors than it declares.
RAISE min_vectors when you add a vector. It is a floor, not an equality:
adding vectors must never require touching four gates.

vectors.name: move_nested_rect_is_1to1
vectors.doc: T1/§3.1 Theseus. Move one rect nested two levels deep. Speaks to the rect's own geometry only; every id in the document survives, and both containers (lyr_main, grp_inner) are bystanders that must come back byte-identical.

vectors.name: delete_bystander_leaf_keeps_containers
vectors.doc: §3.7 / T4. Deleting one leaf ends exactly one identity. The two containers are rebuilt to reach the target — the bystander clause says they must survive the rebuild unchanged.

vectors.name: boolean_union_merges_two_rects
vectors.doc: §3.3 / §3.6 UNION row. N→1: both operand identities die and the result mints a fresh id. Neither operand's id may ride out on the result — 'the frontmost source keeps the id' is the rejected rule, and over-preservation is as much a violation as under-preservation.

vectors.name: wrap_two_rects_in_group
vectors.doc: §3.4 WRAP / T5. The arrow counts material at stake: 0→1 for the new container, 1→1 for each child. Every child id survives; the wrapper's id is the one supplied by the op, and must not duplicate an existing one.

vectors.name: unpack_inner_group
vectors.doc: §3.4 UNWRAP / T5. The container's identity ends; the children keep theirs (both ports' apply_unpack_group_at already say 'children keep their ids — NO minting'). The outer layer is a bystander it must rebuild to reach the group.

vectors.name: blob_paint_into_one_blob_is_1to1
vectors.doc: §3.1 Theseus + T1's RING TERM, driven through the production blob-brush gesture rather than op_apply (the commit arms have no op verb at all). The sweep overlaps blob_left only, so the commit takes the 1-match arm: the element survives with its id, and the ONLY keys that may differ are `d` and `fill_rule` — the latter because the union RE-DERIVED the rings, which is exactly what T1's third closure says such an edit speaks to. blob_right, r_bystander and the container lyr_blob are bystanders. `must_change` names both keys, which is what makes this vector SEPARATE the ring term rather than merely tolerate it: `subject_fields_only` is blind to anything listed in `speaks_to`, so without the claim an arm that carried the source's rule would stay green here (measured: it does).

vectors.name: blob_paint_merges_two_blobs
vectors.doc: §3.3 / the cardinality law, at the arm §4's ratification condition records as having ZERO corpus coverage: 'no gesture fixture reaches the N>=2 merge arm'. One sweep bridges blob_left and blob_right, so both identities die and the result wears exactly one freshly minted id. Neither source's id may ride out — over-preservation is as much a violation as under-preservation. lyr_blob and r_bystander are the bystanders.

vectors.name: blob_paint_beside_everything_creates_without_minting
vectors.doc: The 0 -> 1 arm. The sweep lands where nothing matches, so the commit creates a brand-new blob beside the existing artwork. No creation tool in this app mints an element id (§5.1), so expected_fresh_ids is 0 — and all THREE existing elements plus the container are bystanders, which makes this the widest T4 watch in the family.

vectors.name: compound_operand_dup_id_is_deduped_on_import
vectors.doc: id_uniqueness at the SERIALIZATION BOUNDARY (REFERENCE_GRAPH.md 2.5). The setup SVG is ill-formed on purpose: a live compound shape's OPERAND repeats the id of an earlier tree child. Every document reader runs dedupe_element_ids / dedupeElementIds to establish the invariant on import; those walks descended through group/layer children only, so an operand duplicate rode through untouched and the LOADED document violated the invariant its own reader exists to enforce. The edit here is deliberately trivial (move the bystander rect) - the vector is not about the edit, it is about what the reader handed the edit. Nothing else in the corpus watches the reader this way: id_uniqueness is evaluated on the post-edit document, and a 1:1 move carries an import-time duplicate straight through to it.

vectors.name: lock_a_group_keeps_the_group_itself
vectors.doc: T4 in its purest form. Locking a group speaks to `locked` and nothing else, so the container must come back carrying its own id, name, opacity and transform. Swift's Controller.lockSelection rebuilt the Group from an inline five-argument literal, so the very container the artist locked lost its identity; Rust's lock_element was clone-then-mutate and never had the hole. TURNED BY LOCKMAT, and it pinned the PRE-RULING answer in as many words: this vector used to name r_back and r_front as SUBJECTS, because both ports recursed and stamped `locked = true` onto them. transcripts/LAYER_STRUCTURE.md §13 (RULED by JYH 2026-07-28) makes lock INHERITED, so the descendants of a locked group are exactly what the edit must NOT touch. They are bystanders now, alongside lyr_main and r_bystander, which is a strictly stronger claim than the one this vector made before — a regression to materialization reds it here as well as in operations/lock_selection_no_materialization.json.

vectors.name: unlock_all_keeps_every_container_it_walks
vectors.doc: T4. unlock_all rewrites `locked` on every element in the document, so it rebuilds EVERY container on the way down; each of those containers is a bystander whose own fields must survive. The lock in this vector is put on a LEAF (r_front) so the only container-rebuilding op under test is unlock_all itself, and the lock/unlock pair nets to zero — the document's one real change is the r_bystander nudge, which is what keeps the run from being byte-identical and therefore vacuous.

txns.name: nudge one rect, then lock a leaf and unlock everything

vectors.name: show_all_keeps_every_container_it_walks
vectors.doc: T4. show_all walks the whole document resetting `visibility`, rebuilding every container it passes; those containers are bystanders. The hide is applied to a LEAF (r_front) so show_all is the only container-rebuilding op under test, and hide/show nets to zero — the r_bystander nudge is the document's one real change, so the run is not byte-identical and the invariants are not vacuous.

txns.name: nudge one rect, then hide a leaf and show everything

vectors.name: move_nested_rect_keeps_a_masked_group_and_a_saturated_path
vectors.doc: T4 (the BYSTANDER CLAUSE) over the twelve fields the canonical test JSON could not see until 2026-07-28. Moving r_target rewrites one leaf two levels down, so BOTH bystanders must come back byte-identical -- including grp_masked, the very container an implementation rebuilds to reach the child, which carries a mask (inverted, unlinked, with its own transformed subtree) and a blend mode. Those two fields are exactly what Swift's private `withChildren` and its inline Layer(/Group( literals destroy (section 3.5), and no vector in this corpus could express them before, because every setup came in through SVG and the SVG codec has no counterpart for either. p_dashed carries the rest: blend mode, tool origin, fill rule, an inside-aligned dashed stroke with anchor alignment and a non-default miter limit, a width profile, a stroke brush and its overrides, and both gradients. `bystander_fields_present` makes the saturation a CHECKED claim: a setup that decayed to defaults reds the gate instead of passing on nothing.

vectors.name: show_all_keeps_a_knockout_group
vectors.doc: T4 (the BYSTANDER CLAUSE) over the two CONTAINER-ONLY fields, `isolated_blending` and `knockout_group`. Every other vector in this corpus watches fields a leaf can carry; these two exist only on Group and Layer, so no leaf-shaped vector can reach them, and until 2026-07-28 no codec carried them either -- the law's own gate snapshots canonical test JSON, so an edit that destroyed a group's knockout setting produced byte-identical JSON and passed. `show_all` is chosen as the edit precisely because it walks the WHOLE document resetting `visibility`, rebuilding every container it passes; grp_knockout and lyr_flags are rebuilt while being spoken to about nothing but visibility. A Swift-style field-by-field container rebuild loses both flags exactly there. The hide is applied to a LEAF (r_inside) so show_all is the only container-rebuilding op under test, and hide/show nets to zero -- the r_sibling nudge is the document's one real change, so the run is not byte-identical and the invariants are not vacuous. `bystander_fields_present` makes the setup's saturation a CHECKED claim: before the three codecs carried these flags, the setup decayed to defaults on the way in and this vector red-lit rather than passing on nothing.

txns.name: nudge one rect, then hide a leaf inside the knockout group and show everything
